headline: From an empty Arabic editor to a Russian sample without leaving the workspace
overview: Elena uses real sample text to understand one script, opens the keyboard-aware language switcher, and lands in a second script with another usable sample.
payoff: She has produced visible sample text in both Arabic and Russian and confirmed the matching layouts without installing anything.

scenes.title: Elena starts in a right-to-left workspace
scenes.narrative: The Arabic editor, native layout, speech controls, and physical-keyboard guidance are ready without sign-in. She can see the writing direction before typing a character.
frameCaptions: Elena starts in a right-to-left workspace

scenes.title: A complete Arabic sentence fills the editor
scenes.narrative: One click produces a real Arabic sentence in the right-to-left field. Elena can inspect spacing, letter joining, and the matching on-screen key layout instead of practising against placeholder text.
frameCaptions: A complete Arabic sentence fills the editor

scenes.title: Every other script stays one command away
scenes.narrative: The language picker keeps the Arabic workspace behind it and lists destinations by both English and native names. Switching scripts is a workspace action, not a return to the homepage.
frameCaptions: Every other script stays one command away

scenes.title: The workspace genuinely becomes Russian
scenes.narrative: The route, editor label, direction, help copy, and full on-screen layout now describe Russian. Elena did not merely change a heading over the same keys.

scenes.title: A second script produces a second real sentence
scenes.narrative: The Russian sample fills the editor above its matching Cyrillic keys. Elena has now compared two functioning writing surfaces, not two screenshots in a language menu.
frameCaptions: A second script produces a second real sentence
